NDIA ICT Infrastructure Management Policy
NDIA-POL-ICT-INF-001
Infrastructure, O/S, and Compute
1. Purpose, governance and risk accountability
Infrastructure governance, risk appetite and reporting

NDIA must govern ICT infrastructure through approved accountable roles, risk appetite, internal controls and executive reporting so infrastructure decisions protect participant outcomes, support lawful collaboration, and keep security, availability, cost and lifecycle risks within approved tolerance.
The NDIA must give ICT infrastructure clear owners, manage decisions within approved risk appetite, keep internal controls working, and report material risks, costs and service issues to executives.
Mandatory governance requirement
High

2. Technology lifecycle, authorisation and asset control
Lifecycle management, authorisation, asset stocktake and controlled technology

NDIA must manage each infrastructure system and asset through an ISM-aligned lifecycle from planning and procurement to operation, change and disposal; systems must be authorised or reauthorised before production or material change, recorded in asset and authorised-system registers, comply with applicable Commonwealth technology standards, and restrict prohibited, legacy, smart and IoT technologies unless risk-approved.
The NDIA must keep an accurate register of infrastructure assets and authorised systems, manage them through their full life, and approve new, changed, legacy, smart or IoT technology before use.
Mandatory lifecycle requirement
Critical

3. Procurement, supplier assurance and contract security
Supplier risk, FOCI, security clauses, monitoring and exit

NDIA must procure and manage infrastructure suppliers through risk-based security, privacy, FOCI and financial approval checks; contracts must flow down PSPF, ISM and NDIA security obligations, require assurance evidence and audit rights, control subcontractors, and include monitored service, transition, exit, data return and secure disposal requirements.

The NDIA must assess infrastructure suppliers before engagement, include security and privacy obligations in contracts, monitor supplier performance, control subcontractors, and plan secure transition or exit.
Mandatory supplier assurance requirement
Critical

4. Cloud, hosting, data centre and service management
Cloud governance, HCF/IRAP assurance, data sovereignty, service levels and exit

NDIA cloud, hosting, gateway-hosting and data centre services must use approved government patterns, HCF-certified or otherwise risk-approved providers, current IRAP or required accreditation evidence, defined owners and service levels, approved data residency, portability, monitoring, reliability, cost and exit arrangements before and throughout production use.

The NDIA must use approved cloud, hosting and data centre services only when ownership, security assurance, data location, service levels, monitoring, cost controls and exit arrangements are defined and accepted.
Mandatory cloud and hosting requirement
Critical

5. Information classification, privacy and protected information handling
Classification, protective marking, privacy governance and approved data flows

The NDIA must know what information each infrastructure service holds or moves, classify and protect it correctly, and apply privacy, access, storage, transmission and disclosure controls before use.
Mandatory information protection requirement
Critical

6. Records, retention, FOI, migration and secure disposal

The NDIA must keep required infrastructure records, logs and metadata, make them retrievable, and only delete, migrate, sanitise or dispose of data, media and assets under approved records, privacy and security processes.
